newsitem.title: USA: MORTGAGE-BACKEDS DRIFT BEFORE NEW INFLATION DATA.
newsitem.headline: MORTGAGE-BACKEDS DRIFT BEFORE NEW INFLATION DATA.

text.p: Mortgage-backed securities (MBS) were little changed in tandem with Treasuries at midday Monday, with the markets awaiting direction from retail sales and inflation indicators later in the week.

"Mortgage trade is directional, outperforming Treasuries in a down market and underperforming in an up market," a trader noted. In the absence of a clear-cut path for Treasuries ahead of the new data, "it's just a very treacherous, thin market right now," the trader added.
The 7 1/2-percent MBS were off 1/32 to 2/32 at midday, while 10-year Treasury notes were down 2/32.
The 6.38 percent yield on 10-year Treasury notes at midday was the highest since 6.42 percent at the close on July 2.

That rate upturn has tempered predictions for accelerated MBS prepayments. The 10-year note's yield had briefly fallen as low as 6.00 percent less than two weeks ago, intensifying concerns that homeowners would refinance mortgage loans and MBS would prepay early.
Further evidence of tame inflation, however, could reduce rates and reheat prepayment fears, traders said.

Amid current coupon 7 1/2-percent 30-year MBS, Government National Mortgage Association bonds were down 3/32 at midday Monday, quoted at 100-24/32 for a bond equivalent yield of 7.43 percent. Federal National Mortgage Association bonds were unchanged at 100-28/32 and Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp bonds were off 2/32 at 100-31/32.

When Treasuries plunged Friday, market participants observed up-in-coupon MBS trades and swapping into MBS from Treasuries. There was no price movement Monday morning, in contrast, to differentiate activity in low coupons from high coupons.
Thirty-year MBS with eight percent and higher coupons were unchanged to down 3/32 Monday. The lower coupons were also flat to 3/32 lower on the day.
On Friday, the eight percent and higher coupons were unchanged to 3/8 point lower, whereas lower coupons lost as much as 5/8 point. Ten-year Treasuries on Friday plunged about one point.
